mechanism_narrative: A sustained four-week rise in TRANSIT mobility from -39.1 to -14.0 signals reduced travel fear and restored commuting, which lifts discretionary retail footfall. RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -39.1 to -14.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise above -20 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing above zero from -5.0 to +7.4 indicates normalized essential shopping routines, which spill over into broader retail visits. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > 0 for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at t-1w (7.4) and t-0w (6.9)
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 for two or more weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of recovering TRANSIT and still-depressed WORKPLACES indicates that non-work trips are driving mobility. This leisure-oriented travel lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved to -14.0 while WORKPLACES remained at -29.0
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above -20 and WORKPLACES is below -25 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime with RESIDENTIAL below 3.0, residents are not confined to home, and positive PARKS mobility signals outdoor activity that supports nearby retail. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 2.6 and PARKS is 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains below 3.0 and PARKS stays above 0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the last 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The seasonal transition from summer to autumn reduces park visits, as seen in PARKS falling from 16.3 to 11.9. This shift moves leisure spending indoors toward retail and recreation. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 16.3 at t-1w to 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline by more than 4 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM above 5 signals continued caution and stockpiling, which crowds out discretionary retail spending. RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 6.9 at t-0w and 7.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above 5 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES remaining deeply negative below -25 indicates persistent work-from-home mandates or caution, which suppress weekday retail footfall. RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -29.0 at t-0w and -29.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -25 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT above -20 and PARKS above 0 indicates people are taking more local trips, which directly boosts retail and recreation visits. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -14.0 and PARKS is 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above -20 and PARKS is above 0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than the last 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
